Whitfield Harrington Jr.

American Center candidate for United States Senator, Illinois · Open seat

Pastor in Chicago; formerly worked in banking and insurance and ran his own insurance practice

Whitfield Harrington Jr. is a Chicago pastor who grew up in Belzoni, Mississippi, and now lives in Schaumburg. He founded the American Center Party as a state party and filed with the Illinois State Board of Elections on May 26, 2026, as its U.S. Senate candidate. He is running for the open seat held by retiring Sen. Dick Durbin, against Democrat Juliana Stratton and Republican Don Tracy.

Where Jr. stands

Cost of living
Says his first bill would be a Family Affordability Act. It would require small-dollar mortgages for homes under $100,000, ban excessive speculation in energy markets, end tariffs on food and make the first year of community college free, without raising taxes on working families.
Health care
Supports Direct Primary Care, where patients pay a doctor a monthly fee for unlimited visits with no insurance middleman. He says he has used it himself.
Immigration
Supports securing the border with manpower, technology and physical barriers where they work, and deporting criminals. Supports ending family separations and making legal immigration easier than illegal entry.
Immigration enforcement (ICE)
Supports immigration enforcement, but says ICE must be reined in when its conduct is excessive.
Federal spending
Proposes moving 10–20% of the defense budget, on a two-year cycle, into U.S. infrastructure. Also proposes a Cabinet-level anti-fraud department to recover money he says is lost to fraud each year.
National security
Says no American troops should deploy without a clear mission, cost and exit plan voted on by Congress.
Abortion
Supports abortion rights.
Guns
Supports background checks for gun purchases.
Education
Supports school choice and making the first year of community college free.
Two-party system
Says Washington is broken and both parties helped break it. He is running outside both major parties to build a center-focused party that draws people from the left and the right.

Background

  • Pastor in Chicago (current)
  • Ran his own insurance practice; earlier worked at banks and insurance companies
  • Has never held public office (elected Governor of Mississippi Boys State in 1997)
  • B.A. in political science, Delta State University (Mississippi)
  • Founder of the American Center Party (Illinois state party)
  • Born and raised in Belzoni, Mississippi
